description: Verify that DUT extends the reassembly timer based on the first fragment's TTL — fragment 1 arriving after the static ipIniReassembleTimeout (but within Large-TTL grace) must still be reassembled (RFC 791 §3.2 MAX(TLB, TTL))
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 791 §3.2 says reassembly timeout is MAX(internal-bucket-clock, TTL). A fragment carrying a Large TTL grants the bucket extra time. DUT must honour that and reassemble when the second fragment arrives within the extended window — even if the static timer has already expired.

Note: Linux's static ipfrag_time ignores TTL (see reference_linux_ip_reassembly_deviations.md). On a Linux DUT this case lands as Fail_timeout — that's a known kernel deviation, not a harness bug. Strict-RFC DUTs land Pass.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: fragment 0 with Large TTL (MF=1)
2. Wait > ipIniReassembleTimeout but < (TTL-extended timeout)
3. Tester → DUT: fragment 1 (MF=0)
4. Observation: DUT → Tester Echo Reply matching id/seq/data.

[Pass condition]
DUT reassembles and emits a matching Reply.

[Fail condition]
Fail_echo_id / Fail_echo_seq / Fail_data_mismatch / Fail_timeout — same shape as IPV4_FRAGMENTS_01.

verdicts.Pass: DUT reassembled within TTL-extended window — normal RFC 791 §3.2
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not emit Reply (Linux static timer ignores TTL — kernel deviation, not harness bug)
